story.originalTitle: Why F1 should avoid knee-jerk rule changes after Lando Norris' Madrid heartbreak
story.summaryEn: Lando Norris lost an almost guaranteed win at the Spanish Grand Prix due to the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car triggered by Lance Stroll's retirement on lap 14, and the article argues that F1 should not rush into rule changes because of it.
detailZh: 为什么F1在兰多·诺里斯的马德里心碎之后应该避免仓促修改规则
"这根本不是你应该输掉一场比赛的方式，"这位卫冕世界冠军在错失一场几乎到手的胜利后说道——虽然他提出可能修改规则的问题是合理的，但几乎不存在一个理想的解决方案
兰多·诺里斯输掉了一场一级方程式的比赛胜利，既不是他自己的错，也不是他车队的错，而仅仅是因为一次虚拟安全车的时机不幸——这次虚拟安全车是在西班牙大奖赛第14圈由兰斯·斯特罗尔退赛引发的。这位迈凯伦车手在虚拟安全车启动前仅仅几秒错过了维修区入口——而且他可能是唯一一个因此真正受损的人。他的主要对手们本周末实际上根本无法接近诺里斯的节奏，却趁机完成了一次廉价进站——而最快的人只能屈居第三名。
这听起来不太对劲。因此，在大奖赛结束后，虚拟安全车基本上成了唯一真正的话题，修改规则的可能性再次被提起也是不可避免的。
“作为车手，今天我真的没有任何办法把工作做得更好，”诺里斯在比赛结束几分钟后于新闻发布会上说。“拿下杆位，领跑比赛，最后却因为我无法控制的原因输掉，我不认为比赛应该是这样取胜的。
“但我认为人们……我希望人们会同意，我认为人们会同意的。但这就是赛车，事情已经发生了，所以我实在没什么好抱怨的。我可以为此感到难过，但我真的不能抱怨。”
现在很容易就宣称规则需要修改——而且在这类情况中经常如此，你会听到很多“简单的解决方案”，在比赛结果的不公平被清晰地展示出来之后，这些方案不知怎的显得过于显而易见。
而这样的方案至少有两个，诺里斯本人在同一场新闻发布会上也提到了。
“我们过去已经谈过这个问题好几次了，谈的是如何至少能保证一圈的覆盖，或者让所有人都有机会完成进站，或者干脆封锁进站口，谁都不能进站，除非你爆胎之类的，你懂的。”
“所以，我认为有几种办法可以让这件事变得更简单、对每个人都更公平，但那是一个更大的讨论话题。”
这两个方案听起来都不错。但实际上，这两个方案都同样没用。
在虚拟安全车（VSC）期间关闭维修通道，或者允许所有人进站，在马德里本来会非常有效，这一点毫无疑问。
由于比赛中不允许加油，在虚拟安全车期间其实没有太大必要允许进站。就算虚拟或真实安全车出场时机不佳，赛车也不会突然耗尽燃油，所以只要关闭维修区入口，就能消除规则中一些“不公平”的因素。
如果维修区保持关闭，诺里斯就不会吃亏——因为没有人能够借机获得一次廉价的进站。
那么问题解决了吗？并没有。原因就在于当初为什么需要安全车——或其虚拟形式：大多数情况下，安全车出动是因为赛道上发生了事故。当赛道上可能还有一辆甚至几辆赛车靠着三个轮子慢行或前翼受损时，关闭维修区显然既不合逻辑也不安全。
西班牙大奖赛并不是第一场虚拟安全车影响了比赛结果的比赛。
只允许受损赛车进站也会有很大问题——因为你需要在体育规则中以某种方式定义“损坏”。像皮亚斯特里在马德里那次前翼受损，算不算符合在虚拟安全车（VSC）下进站的“足够”标准？如果再夸张一点想，车手们是不是还会故意去扎胎，以此获得进站的权利？
这只会制造太多灰色地带——其中最明显的一条，连诺里斯本人都提到了。
“我觉得，作为车手群体，我们都希望有这样一个规则，”他说，但同时也承认“这里面还有很多复杂的问题”。
“你知道，如果当时下着雨，赛道上有虚拟安全车（VSC），而你还用的是干地胎，这是不是意味着你可以进站，还是不能？这是个很复杂的问题。”
当然，出于安全考虑启用虚拟安全车，然后却不允许使用光头胎的车手换上雨胎，这显然与采取该措施的目的自相矛盾。如果这是一个合适的解决方案，早就被采用了。问题在于，事情并不像马德里站之后看起来那么简单。
整圈虚拟安全车也不是解决方案
那么，另一个选择是确保所有车手都有机会进站——这确实是一个简单的解决办法。因为真正对诺里斯不利的原因，并不是虚拟安全车在他已经驶过维修区入口时才启动——而是等他跑完一圈回到那里时，赛道已经恢复绿灯了。
为什么不确保虚拟安全车至少持续一整圈，让每个人都有机会便宜地进站换胎呢？
国际汽联的赛事总监和车手们当然可以在下一站巴库的会议上就此进行辩论——但即使他们真的讨论了，也很可能很快得出结论：这同样不是解决办法。虽然这样做可以再次确保西班牙大奖赛有一个“公平”的结果，但重要的是要记住，它只涵盖这一个特定场景——在其他情况下反而可能让事情变得更糟。
正因为一级方程式中仍然存在不同的策略，几乎总是会有车手因为安全车出现的时机而受益——也总会有车手因此吃亏。
有一个明确的场景，如果规则——以及比赛本身——稍有不同，就会对诺里斯不利。假设迈凯伦车手在第12圈进站，例如是为了防止梅赛德斯的基米·安东内利尝试抢先进站超越。这是完全正常的操作——而那位意大利车手接下来的可能策略就是延后自己的进站，以制造更大的轮胎差距。
如果诺里斯进站之后出现任何虚拟安全车，他将面临被安东内利夺走位置的风险。而在这种情况下，确保虚拟安全车至少持续一圈，实际上反而会保证并巩固“不公平”的结果——原因很简单：梅赛德斯将默认获得一次低成本进站，无论马修们清理事故的速度有多快。而在那种情况下，那些追求简单解决方案的人很可能会大声抱怨赛事控制必须尽快采取行动。
现实情况是，体育层面的结果——或者说何时以及多长时间出动安全车的问题——根本不会被比赛控制中心纳入考量。而且这样做是对的。赛车运动仍然是一项危险的运动，在做出这些决定时，安全应该是唯一的优先事项。
“但我认为，作为一个车手群体，如果我们大家都来讨论这件事，我想每个人都想要同样的东西，那就是对每个人的公平，”诺里斯说。“所以，是的，我今天当然要抱怨这件事。下周、下一场比赛我可能反而会从中受益，并因此获胜。
“所以，是的，我只能接受这个结果，但我只是希望这种事不要再发生在任何人身上，因为你不应该以这种方式输掉一场比赛。”
基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯；兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦
但是，虽然车手们当然可以畅所欲言并提出关切，这并不意味着媒体上出现“诺里斯呼吁修改规则”这类头条新闻就必然需要立即采取行动。
对于这个问题，也许只有一个非常简单的解决办法——接受体育并不总是“公平”的这一事实。
这并不意味着不应该进行讨论，因为马德里暴露了一个早已为人所知的问题。但这个问题之所以长期存在，恰恰是因为没有简单的修复办法。
那些提出简单解决方案的人通常属于两种类型之一：真正不理解问题的人，或者是政客。
detailEn: Why F1 should avoid knee-jerk rule changes after Lando Norris' Madrid heartbreak

"It’s just not how you should lose a race," said the reigning world champion after missing out on an almost guaranteed victory - and while he's right to raise the question of potential rule changes, there is hardly an ideal solution

Lando Norris lost a Formula 1 race win through no fault of his own - or his team's - but simply because of the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car, triggered on lap 14 of the Spanish Grand Prix after Lance Stroll's retirement. The McLaren driver missed the pitlane entry by mere seconds before the VSC was activated - and was probably the only man to really lose out because of it. His main rivals, who weren't actually even close to matching Norris' pace this weekend, got a cheap stop - and the fastest man had to settle for P3.

That doesn't sound quite right. So it was inevitable that the topic of potential rule changes came up again in the aftermath of a grand prix in which the VSC largely became the only real talking point.

“There’s literally nothing I could do as a driver today to do a better job," said Norris a few minutes after the finish in the press conference. "Pole, led the race, and to lose it for nothing in my control is, I don’t think, how a race should be won.

“But I think people... I hope people agree, I think people would agree. But it is racing and it’s happened, so I can’t really complain about it. I can be upset about it, but I can’t really complain about it.”

It's rather tempting now to declare that the rules need changing - and, as often in these sorts of cases, you'll hear a lot of "easy solutions", which somehow seem too obvious after a clear example of how unfair the outcome of the race was.
And there are at least two of that nature, which Norris himself mentioned during the same press conference.

"We have spoken about it in the past several times, about how it can be at least covered for one lap or everyone has the opportunity to do the pit stops, or you just block the pit entry and no one can box apart from if you have a puncture or something, you know.
“So, I think there’s a few things you could do to make it more simple and more fair for everyone, but that’s a bigger discussion.”
Both seem like good options. In reality, though, both are equally useless.
Closing the pitlane under VSC or allowing everyone to stop would have worked perfectly in Madrid, there's no doubt about that.

With no refuelling, there's less need to actually allow pitstops during the VSC. Cars won't suddenly run out of fuel in the event of unfortunate timing of a virtual or real safety car, so simply closing the pitlane entry would eliminate some of the "unfair" elements of the rules.
Had the pitlane stayed closed, Norris wouldn't have lost out - as no one would have been able to get a cheap stop.

Sorted, then? Not quite. Simply because of the reason why there is a need for a safety car - or its virtual analogue - in the first place: more often than not, it happens because of accidents on track. Closing the pitlane while there might be a car - or a few of them - crawling down the track on three wheels or with front wing damage is simply illogical and unsafe.
The Spanish GP wasn't the first race in which a VSC affected the result

Allowing only cars with damage to pit would also be problematic - as you'd need to somehow define damage within the sporting regulations. Would damage like that to Oscar Piastri's front wing in Madrid qualify as "enough" for a pitstop under VSC? If you exaggerate it even further, wouldn't drivers then seek to get a puncture, too - to earn the right to pit?
That would simply create too many grey areas - with the most obvious one mentioned by Norris himself, too.
"I think it’s something, as a group of drivers, I think we would all want," he said, but also admitted that "there’s a lot more to it".
"You know, depending on if it’s raining and there’s a VSC and you’re on slicks, does it mean you can box or not? It’s a complicated subject.”

Certainly, to deploy a VSC for the sake of safety and then disallow drivers on slicks from changing tyres to wets would simply contradict the purpose of the action. And if that was a suitable solution, it would've been implemented a long time ago. The issue is, it's just not as straightforward as it seems after Madrid.
A full-lap VSC isn't the solution either

Then, the other option is to make sure all drivers have a chance to pit - and that is indeed an easy fix. Because what really played against Norris was not the fact that the VSC was activated when he had already driven past the pitlane entry - but that by the time he made his way around the lap, it was already green again.
Why not make sure a VSC lasts for at least one lap, so everyone gets a chance for a cheap stop?

That's a debate FIA race directors and drivers can certainly have during the next meeting in Baku - but even if they do, they'd probably quickly come to the conclusion that it's not a solution either. While it would, again, guarantee a "fair" outcome of the Spanish Grand Prix, it's important to remember it covers only this particular scenario - and potentially makes things even worse in others.
Just because different strategies in F1 still exist, there are almost always going to be those benefiting from the lucky timing of a safety car - and those hard done by it.

There's one clear scenario which would have played against Norris had the rules - and the race itself - been slightly different. Say the McLaren driver had pitted on lap 12 of the race to, for example, prevent an undercut attempt from Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes. That would be something perfectly normal to do - and the possible strategy for the Italian would then be delaying his stop to create a bigger tyre delta.

Any VSC after Norris' stop would put him in danger of losing the position to Antonelli. And in this case, making sure the VSC lasts at least one lap would actually guarantee and secure the "unfair" outcome - simply because Mercedes would get a cheap pitstop by default, irrespective of how quickly the marshals cleared the incident. And in that case, those seeking easy solutions would probably be vocal about race control needing to act as quickly as possible.

The reality is that the sporting outcome - or the question of when and for how long to deploy a safety car - simply isn't taken into account by race control. And rightly so. Motor racing is still a dangerous sport, and safety is the only priority there should be when making these calls.

“But I think as a collection of drivers, if we all talk about it, I think everyone wants the same thing, and that’s just fairness for everyone," said Norris. "So yeah, of course I’m complaining about it today. I could benefit from it next week, next time out, and I could win because of it.
“So yeah, I have to take it on the chin, but I just hope it doesn’t happen to anyone again because it’s just not how you should lose a race.”
Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lando Norris, McLaren
But while drivers are surely free to speak their minds and raise concerns, it doesn't mean headlines in the media about "Norris calls for rule changes" should necessarily require immediate action.
Perhaps there is just one really simple solution to this problem - to accept that sport isn't always "fair".
It doesn't mean there shouldn't be a discussion, as Madrid highlighted a long-known issue. But it's also long-known precisely because there's no simple way to fix it.
Those offering simple solutions are usually one of two types: people who don't really understand the problem, or politicians.

detailZh: F1美国大奖赛：汉密尔顿在FP3中险胜维斯塔潘
法拉利在COTA的每节练习中都排名第一，进入排位赛
汉密尔顿在F1美国大奖赛的最后一节练习中排名第一，领先维斯塔潘和勒克莱尔进入奥斯汀的排位赛
在第三节的最后20分钟里，汉密尔顿是唯一打破1分35秒大关的车手，频繁的越界行为使得法拉利队友勒克莱尔无法超越他登上排行榜。
本节练习的前三圈只能用平淡无奇来形容，但随着汉密尔顿在软胎上跑出1分36.716秒，超越了多个使用中等轮胎的圈速。
不久后，小红牛车队和迈凯轮的利亚姆·劳森打破了汉密尔顿的成绩，而几位重量级选手仍在使用中等轮胎进行圈速测试。
尽管范斯特appen对换挡时的不稳定状态有所抱怨，但他凭借黄色侧壁轮胎的1分35.702秒成绩名列前茅。
汉密尔顿迅速提升了成绩，使用软胎跑出了1分35.561秒。但勒克莱尔尽管使用的是较慢的中胎，却以1分35.127秒的成绩接管了领先位置，这表明还有更多的速度可以挖掘。
进入最后20分钟，安东内利在软胎上比勒克莱尔快了十分之一，但他在9号弯道超出了赛道限制，导致这一圈被取消。
维斯塔潘遵守了白线，以1分35.061秒的成绩排名第一，红牛车队在第一区段是最快的，但汉密尔顿的成绩低于1分35秒，达到了1分34.893秒。
在整个练习过程中一直出现的赛道限制问题，也阻止了勒克莱尔重新夺回第一的位置，因为他在10号弯道越过了白线。
这意味着摩纳哥车手只能满足于排在汉密尔顿和维斯塔潘之后，为周六下午的排位赛设置了一场紧张激烈的局面。
冠军车手安东内利排在第四位，领先于梅赛德斯车队的队友乔治·拉塞尔，银箭车队似乎在纯速度上落后半步，皮亚斯蒂在难以驾驭的MCL40中排在第六位。
在奥迪车队，尼科·胡肯伯格阻止了麦克拉伦车队的兰多·诺里斯获得第七名，世界冠军的1分35.2秒成绩也因为第十弯的赛道限制而被取消。
阿尔派车队的皮埃尔·加斯利排在第九位，落后汉密尔顿一秒，伊萨克·哈德贾在第二辆小红牛车队中排在第十位，这位法国车手因为他的赛车操控问题而感到沮丧。
detailEn: F1 United States GP: Lewis Hamilton pips Max Verstappen in FP3
Ferrari heads into qualifying having topped every practice session at COTA
Lewis Hamilton finished final practice on top at Formula 1's United States Grand Prix, leading Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc into qualifying at Austin.

Hamilton was the only driver to break the 1m35s barrier in the final 20 minutes of third practice, as frequent track limits transgressions kept Ferrari team-mate Leclerc from leapfrogging him on the leaderboard.
Following an opening quarter of the session which can only be described as pedestrian, action picked up as Hamilton set a 1m36.716s on softs to get ahead of a number of medium-tyred install laps.
His time was soon beaten by Liam Lawson in the Racing Bulls and McLaren's Oscar Piastri, while several heavy hitters kept turning laps on medium tyres instead.
Verstappen even went top courtesy of a 1m35.702s on the yellow sidewall tyre, despite recurring complaints about his unsettling downshifts.

Hamilton swiftly improved upon the Dutchman's lap, using softs to set a 1m35.561s. But when Leclerc took over command with a 1m35.127s despite using the slower mediums, that underlined there was still a lot more pace to find.
Entering the final 20 minutes, Antonelli took a tenth out of Leclerc's time on softs, but his lap was scratched for breaking track limits at Turn 9.
Verstappen did adhere to the white lines to set a 1m35.061s and go top, with Red Bull the quickest car through sector one, only for Hamilton to dip below the 1m35s barrier with a 1m34.893s.
Track limits, which have been a recurring theme throughout practice, also kept Leclerc from reclaiming first as he dipped over the white line at Turn 10.
That meant the Monegasque had to settle for third behind Hamilton and Verstappen, setting up a finely poised qualifying session on Saturday afternoon.

Championship leader Antonelli was fourth ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell, as the Silver Arrows appears to be a half-step behind on pure pace, with Piastri sixth in the difficult to tame MCL40.
In the Audi, Nico Hulkenberg kept McLaren’s Lando Norris from seventh, with the world champion’s 1m35.2s also deleted for track limits at Turn 10.
Alpine driver Pierre Gasly was ninth, a full second behind Hamilton, with Isack Hadjar 10th in the second Red Bull as the Frenchman was left frustrated by his car's handling.
keyPointsZh: 勒克莱尔因越界无法超越汉密尔顿
keyPointsEn: Leclerc could not overtake Hamilton due to track limits transgressions

detailZh: 丹尼尔·里卡多在美国大奖赛前夕的现场表演令F1粉丝感到惊喜
前F1车手丹尼尔·里卡多与音乐家罗布·贝尔德一起吹奏口琴，令粉丝感到惊喜
丹尼尔·里卡多，Drive to Survive第七季
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事。
前一级方程式车手丹尼尔·里卡多在美国德克萨斯州奥斯汀的舞台上出现了一个惊喜。
这位澳大利亚人与歌手兼词曲作者罗布·贝尔德一起加入了福特赛车和Enchanté快闪活动，在周五晚上一起演奏他与美国大奖赛旅途中共创作的原创歌曲。
一位粉丝在Instagram上发布的表演视频，截至写作时已经获得了超过7000个赞。一位粉丝评论说：“这治愈了我心中的某一部分，”另一位粉丝补充说：“我敢打赌他上辈子要么是鲍勃·迪伦的兄弟，要么是个牛仔哈哈。我们爱你，丹尼尔。”
“在这个时候，没有人关心比赛。很高兴看到丹尼尔回来了，即使他不再赛车，”另一位粉丝写道，另一位粉丝写道：“作为一个音乐家和蜜獾粉丝，和丹尼·里卡多一起演奏是我的梦想。”
“我是说真的很长的一段路。沙漠、乡村小道、游泳洞，所有这些。说实话，我迫不及待了。”
这次长途旅行是推广新系列 Enchanté Collection 的活动之一，名为《长途》。这些新产品在奥斯汀的 Distribution Hall 的临时展位上出售，展位上还有食品、饮料、闪粉纹身和赛车模拟器。
里卡多也被看到在支持 小红牛 车队的车手利亚姆·劳森，作为新西兰人，他在 Esses Bazaar ATX 活动中担任主角，与利亚姆·劳森和朋友们一起在东第六街的 Inn Cahoots 举办车库音乐会，此次活动是为本周末的美国大奖赛做准备。
detailEn: Daniel Ricciardo surprises F1 fans with on-stage performance ahead of US GP
Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo surprised fans with a harmonica performance alongside musician Rob Baird
Daniel Ricciardo , Drive to Survive Season 7
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo made a surprise appearance on stage in Austin, Texas, with American singer-songwriter Rob Baird.
The Australian joined Baird at the Ford Racing and Enchanté pop-up on Friday night to play harmonica on an original song he co-wrote with Baird during a road trip to the United States Grand Prix.

A fan video of the performance, posted on Instagram, had picked up more than 7000 likes by the time of writing. "This healed something in me," one fan commented, while another added: "I'm sure he was either Bob Dylan's brother or a cowboy in a previous life lol. We love you, Daniel."

"At this point, no one cares about the race. Glad to see Daniel back, even if he’s not racing," someone else posted, and another fan wrote: "As a musician and a honey badger fan, it would be a dream to play with Danny Ric."
"And I mean the lonnnng way. Desert, backroads, swimming holes, all of it. Not gonna lie, I can't wait."

The road trip was part of the promotion of the new Enchanté collection, The Long Road. The new products are being sold at a pop-up at Distribution Hall in Austin alongside food, drinks, flash tattoos and racing simulators.

Ricciardo was also spotted supporting Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson as the New Zealander headlined Garage Sessions with Liam Lawson and Friends as part of Esses Bazaar ATX, held at Inn Cahoots on East Sixth Street ahead of this weekend's United States Grand Prix.

relatedItems.originalTitle: Nico Hulkenberg left red-faced after Gabriel Bortoleto prank at United States GP
detailZh: 尼科·胡肯伯格在美国大奖赛上被加布里埃尔·博特洛托恶作剧后颜面扫地
加布里埃尔·博特洛托在美国大奖赛期间的一次粉丝见面会上玩了一个意外的恶作剧，让他的奥迪车队队友笑得前仰后合
赛车文化超越赛道。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事
年轻的奥迪车手加布里埃尔·博特洛托在美洲赛道前与队友尼科·胡肯伯格走在一起时，对他进行了一次恶作剧。两位车手在奥斯汀观众的欢呼声中走出，巴西人拉下了队友的裤子。
这个时刻的视频已经迅速走红，展示了胡肯伯格在周五如何走上舞台，当时博尔特洛从后面抓住他的裤子并将其拉下，引发了观众的欢呼和笑声。这位德国人对此玩笑表示宽容，一边笑着一边整理好衣服。
这个恶作剧为博尔特洛艰难的周末带来了一些轻松。巴西人在周日美国大奖赛将从最后一排发车，因为奥迪为他提供的动力单元组件超出了分配额度。
博尔特洛和胡肯伯格自2025年以来一直是队友，当时车队还以萨博的身份参赛，尽管车队已被德国巨头奥迪接管，但他们成为了赛场上更为轻松的搭档之一。然而，车队在2026年很难获得积分。车队在车队积分榜上排名第八，积分为23分，胡肯伯格积13分，博尔特洛积10分。
博尔特洛在美国大奖赛周末赛前表示：“我在可靠性方面看到了很多改进。显然，我们在新加坡显然有一个问题，我们相信我们已经找到了原因。”
“这显然不是理想的情况，但与此同时，它发生的时候我并没有在前面真正地竞争，所以这让我对它稍微不那么沮丧。但我希望我们能够在接下来的赛季中没有任何重大问题，并且能够以最佳状态完成比赛和排位赛，驾驶我们能够驾驶的最好的汽车，从中提取一切。”
detailEn: Nico Hulkenberg left red-faced after Gabriel Bortoleto prank at United States GP
Gabriel Bortoleto left his Audi team-mate laughing after pulling an unexpected prank during a fan appearance at the United States Grand Prix
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.

Young Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto played a prank on his team-mate Nico Hulkenberg as the pair walked out in front of thousands of fans at the Circuit of the Americas. With both drivers walking out to cheers from the Austin crowds, the Brazilian pulled down his team-mate's trousers.

Videos of this moment have gone incredibly viral, showing Hulkenberg making his way onto the stage on Friday when Bortoleto grabbed his trousers from behind and pulled them down, to loud cheers and laughter from the crowd. The German took the joke in good humour, laughing as he pulled his clothes straight.

The prank offered some light relief on a tough weekend for Bortoleto. The Brazilian will start Sunday’s United States Grand Prix from the back of the grid, after Audi took him beyond his allocation of power unit components.

Bortoleto and Hulkenberg have been team-mates since 2025, when the team still raced as Sauber, and have formed one of the more light-hearted partnerships on the grid despite it being taken over by German giant Audi. The outfit has found points hard to come by in 2026, however. The team is eighth in the constructors’ championship on 23 points, with the experienced Hulkenberg on 13 and Bortoleto on 10.

"I have seen lots of improvement on reliability," Bortoleto said on Thursday ahead of the United States Grand Prix race weekend. "I think we had one [issue] in Singapore obviously, that we believe we found the reason of.

"It was obviously something not ideal to happen, but at the same time it happened when I was not really fighting at the front, so made me a little bit less upset about it. But I hope we are able to do the rest of the season without having any major issue and that we are able to just complete the races and qualifying in the best condition and the best car possible out there that we can drive and extract everything from it."
